useCase.name: Confirm that what the books say was received matches what the bank and gateway actually received

intent.name: finance.reconciliation.start
intent.summary: Open a reconciliation for a bank or gateway account and a period, carrying the opening balance from the last signed-off one. One step, and it changes no book.

routesHere.text: bank account ka milan karna hai
routesHere.gloss: we need to reconcile the bank account

routesElsewhere.note: The reconciliation is opened first, then the statement is imported into it.
Reading the books is a different act from checking them against a statement.

steps.note: One step. The opening balance is carried from the previous signed-off reconciliation and is never typed (BR-11) — and a period cannot be reconciled before the one before it is closed (E6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An unsigned previous period is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the reconciliation at In progress, with its opening balance carried forward and any unresolved differences from the previous period carried with it (BR-11). Nothing in the books changes — reconciliation never adjusts the books to match the statement (BR-1).

intent.name: finance.reconciliation.statement.import
intent.summary: Import a bank or gateway statement into an open reconciliation and match what it can automatically. One step.

routesHere.text: gateway ka settlement file laga do

routesHere: load the statement and run the auto-match

request.gloss: key the statement in by hand

routesElsewhere.note: Statements are imported rather than keyed wherever the format allows. A statement typed by hand is a second place for an error to enter (BR-3).

steps.note: One step. The file is uploaded on the screen and referenced here — the request channel carries no file. Auto-matching runs inside the import.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An unreadable file, a statement covering a different period and lines matching two movements equally well are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors or as unmatched items.
plan.atomicity: One write: the statement lines and the automatic matches, together with the audit entry or not at all. Nothing in the books changes — reconciliation never adjusts the books to match the statement (BR-1). Every unmatched line and every unmatched movement is reported, because a recorded movement with no statement line is how a payment recorded but never received comes to light (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Never key a statement. Import it (BR-3) — a statement typed by hand is a second place for an error to enter, and the whole exercise exists to catch errors.

Never resolve an ambiguous match. Two movements matching one line equally well is left for a person (E3), because a wrongly matched line is worse than an unmatched one — it hides a difference rather than showing it (BR-5).

Report both kinds of unmatched item. A statement line with no movement and a movement with no statement line are different problems, and the second is how a payment recorded but never received comes to light (BR-8).

Never adjust the books to close the difference. Reconciliation confirms; it never adjusts (BR-1), and the difference is itemised line by line rather than forced to zero by an entry nobody can explain (BR-9).

reversal.statement: An import is not undone as a whole, but individual matches can be unmade through finance.reconciliation.match — a wrongly matched line is worse than an unmatched one (BR-5). Nothing in the books has changed.

Never adjust a record to make it match. Where the record was wrong rather than the statement, a correction is raised through UC-04-12 (BR-7) — with its own approval, because it moves money between accounts.

intent.name: finance.reconciliation.signoff
intent.summary: Sign off a reconciliation, with every unmatched item carrying what was done about it. School Admin only, one step, and it cannot be reopened.

routesHere.text: September ki reconciliation sign off kar do
milan mukammal ho gaya, band kar do
routesHere.gloss: the reconciliation is complete, close it

routesHere: close off the gateway settlement reconciliation

routesElsewhere.note: A signed-off reconciliation is not reopened. A later discovery is handled in the current period, since reopening a signed period changes a figure somebody has already relied on (BR-12, E7).
Differences may remain at sign-off, provided each carries what was done about it and a written note (BR-6, A6).

steps.note: One step, and it is terminal. Every unmatched item must already carry an action and a note — nothing is left unexplained simply because the period closed (BR-6, E4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Unexplained items, an unitemised difference and whether the acting user performed the reconciliation themselves are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the sign-off and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing in the books changes. The period becomes closed to further matching and cannot be reopened (BR-12) — unresolved differences carry forward into the next period with their explanations (BR-11).

operations.name: finance.reconciliation.signoff
operations.idempotencyKey: reconciliation_id, since a reconciliation is signed off once and Signed off is terminal
operations.purpose: Sign off a reconciliation, closing the period and carrying any unresolved differences forward.

parameters.name: reconciliation_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No reconciliation matches at a status that allows this.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with account, period, status and outstanding difference.

parameters.notes: The reconciliation, resolved from how the actor named it — the account and period, or simply the one in progress.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: reconciliation_id
fields.description: The reconciliation.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Signed off. Terminal — it is not reopened (BR-12).

fields.name: signed_off_by
fields.description: The School Admin, never the person who performed it (BR-10).

fields.name: difference
fields.description: The gap, itemised.

fields.name: carried_forward
fields.description: Unresolved items and their explanations, carried into the next period (BR-11).

fields.name: closing_balance
fields.description: Becomes the next period's opening balance (BR-11).

errors.meaning: Items are left unmatched with no action or note.
errors.note: The message names the count. Nothing is left unexplained simply because the period closed (BR-6).

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to sign off their own reconciliation.
errors.note: Somebody checking their own work is not a control (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The reconciliation has already been signed off.
errors.note: A signed-off reconciliation is not reopened. A later discovery is handled in the current period (BR-12).

errors.meaning: The difference is not explained line by line.
errors.note: It is never forced to zero by an adjusting entry nobody can explain (BR-9).

planningRules.rule: Never sign off a reconciliation the acting user performed. E5 is BR-10 working — somebody checking their own work is not a control.

Never write the explanations to get past ITEMS_UNEXPLAINED. Each unmatched item carries what was done about it and a written note by the person who investigated it (BR-6) — a note a planner composed explains nothing.
Never treat a remaining difference as a failure. Differences may remain at sign-off provided each is explained (A6), and they carry forward with the opening balance (BR-11).
Never attempt to reopen a signed period. A later discovery is handled in the current period, because reopening changes a figure somebody has already relied on (BR-12, E7).
Report what carries forward. The next period opens with those differences still unexplained, and whoever reconciles it will meet them again.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Signed off is terminal and a signed period is never reopened (BR-12). A later discovery is handled in the current period — as a correction, a voucher, or a difference carried into the open reconciliation. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.
